claims.claim: Grok 4.6 is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output against Claude Fable 5 Max at $10/$50 — an 80% discount on input and 88% on output.
Artificial Analysis puts Grok 4.6 at 61 on its Intelligence Index against Fable 5 Max's 62 — approximately 98.4% of the composite score.
Grok 4.6 ranks #1 on Artificial Analysis' separate Agentic Index, a placement that entered circulation through a relayed reading rather than Artificial Analysis' own post.
Parametric CAD Bench measured Grok 4.6 at 96.9% of Claude Opus 5's top score of 0.906 for 61% of the cost, on the same 100 tasks.
On the same fixed 100 CAD tasks, the cost to exceed a 0.8 score fell from $170.00 to $36.59 in 90 days — a 4.6x deflation in the price of a fixed capability level.
Grok 4.6's GDPVal-AA v2 score of 1,753 places it ahead of Claude Fable 5 Max on real-world agentic knowledge work.
The only third-party leaderboard placement circulating on launch day put Grok 4.6 13th on Frontend Arena at 1,553 points.
A Grok-friendly account (@scaling01) said on launch day that on 'really long-running and autonomous workflows the best OpenAI and Anthropic models are much better in the tails.'
Grok 4.6 ships with a seven-day double-token promotion running to roughly 19 August; whether the $2/$6 price survives the promotion is unconfirmed.
Grok 4.6 went live around 15:27 UTC on 12 August 2026, available same-day in Cursor and Grok Build with 2x usage included for the first week.
GLM-5.2 cost $982.90 to run the full Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index on 140M tokens against Opus 4.8's $4,012 — collapsing its advertised 5.7x output-price edge to a measured 4.1x.
Qwen3.8-Max, priced identically to Grok 4.6 at $2/$6, cost $2,159.51 to complete the AA Intelligence Index on 150M output tokens against a 63M comparison median.
